questions.q: On a map of the Central Coast, which county lies between Monterey and Santa Barbara?
questions.exp: The Court's three Central Coast counties run north to south as Monterey, San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara. San Luis Obispo holds hot, inland Paso Robles, its major AVA, with the cool coastal valleys of Edna Valley and Arroyo Grande by the sea; Santa Barbara is the southernmost, with the city of the same name on its southern shore.

questions.q: The Court's Central Coast runs from the city of Santa Barbara north to the southern shore of which bay?
questions.exp: The Court defines the Central Coast as the coastal counties south of San Francisco Bay and north of the city of Santa Barbara, the stretch the umbrella Central Coast AVA of 1985 covers. It is not the Central Valley, the hot, irrigated interior that grows the everyday wine.

questions.q: In which county does the Court place the Santa Lucia Highlands AVA?
questions.exp: The Santa Lucia Highlands, an AVA of 1991, are terraces on the western side of Monterey County's Salinas Valley, facing east above the valley floor in the afternoon wind and fog: dark, lush Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and cool Syrah. Paso Robles is the Court's San Luis Obispo AVA, and Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Maria Valley, Santa Ynez Valley and Happy Canyon its Santa Barbara four.

questions.q: Besides Paso Robles, which AVA does the Court class as warm among the Central Coast names it lists?
questions.exp: Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara, an AVA of 2009, sits at the hot eastern end of the Santa Ynez Valley beyond the reach of the fog, and grows Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc. Because Santa Barbara's valleys run east to west, the western end is the cold one, so Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Maria Valley and the Santa Lucia Highlands are the Court's cool Pinot Noir and Chardonnay country.

questions.q: Which mountain range shuts Paso Robles off from the ocean on its western side?
questions.exp: The Santa Lucia Range runs along the coast between Paso Robles and the Pacific, which is why the Court calls Paso warm and continental, blocked by mountains with only a small gap in the range. That gap, the Templeton Gap, lets the afternoon sea air into the western hills and gives the AVA its wide swing between hot days and cold nights.

questions.q: Which secondary fermentation does the Court say is often used for Central Coast Chardonnay?
questions.exp: Malolactic fermentation turns sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid and leaves the buttery note of diacetyl, which, with barrel fermentation in new French and sometimes American oak, gives the classic rich Californian Chardonnay. The Santa Barbara houses that pick early for tension often allow only part of it, so the style runs from creamy to taut.

questions.q: Besides Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc, which white grape is a speciality of Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara?
questions.exp: Happy Canyon is warm enough to ripen the Bordeaux grapes fully, and its ripe, grassy Sauvignon Blanc is as prized as its Cabernet. The Court asks the grapes matched to the AVAs: Chardonnay and Pinot Noir to the cool Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Maria Valley and Santa Lucia Highlands, Cabernet and Zinfandel to Paso Robles.

questions.q: Old Zinfandel and Rhône blends draw the attention, but which red grape covers the most ground in Paso Robles?
questions.exp: Cabernet Sauvignon is the most planted grape in Paso Robles, ripe and generous from the warm eastern plain and firmer from the limestone hills of the west side, where Justin built its reputation. Zinfandel is the heritage red of the dry farmed old vines, and Tablas Creek's Rhône cuttings made the GSM blends famous.

questions.q: A Santa Maria Valley Pinot Noir names the Bien Nacido Vineyard on its label. What minimum share of its grapes must come from that vineyard?
questions.exp: A vineyard designation needs 95 per cent of the fruit from the named site, the same figure as a vintage date on an AVA wine. Bien Nacido, planted in 1973, sells fruit to so many houses that its name appears on labels across the state, each held to that 95 per cent; the AVA itself, Santa Maria Valley, needs only 85.

questions.q: Ridge Vineyards, the first of the Court's named Central Coast examples, matures its Monte Bello Cabernet in barrels of which oak, unusual for a top Californian red?
questions.exp: Ridge matures Monte Bello, like its other wines, in air-dried American oak rather than the French oak most of California's grandest Cabernets are raised in, and its 1971 still placed fifth at the Paris tasting of 1976 and first at the rematch of 2006. Monte Bello grows high above Cupertino in the Santa Cruz Mountains AVA; Ridge's Zinfandels, Lytton Springs and Geyserville, come from Sonoma.

questions.q: Justin Vineyards, one of the Court's named examples, made its reputation with the Bordeaux blend Isosceles in which AVA?
questions.exp: Justin farms the limestone hills of the west side of Paso Robles, in what is now the Adelaida District, and Isosceles, a Cabernet-led Bordeaux blend, gave the AVA its first national reputation for Cabernet. Ridge in the Santa Cruz Mountains and Au Bon Climat in the Santa Maria Valley are the Court's other two examples.

questions.q: Au Bon Climat, founded in 1982 and one of the Court's named examples, built its name on which pair of grapes?
questions.exp: Au Bon Climat, at Bien Nacido in the Santa Maria Valley, makes Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in the Burgundian manner, its name borrowing the Burgundian word climat for a named site, and it helped put Santa Barbara County on the map. Its neighbour Qupé, founded the same year, took the Syrah and the Rhône whites.
